author: Elijah
title: Suncorp Bank announces major change to payments in Australia
text:
By Zak Wheeler and Padraig Collins for Daily Mail Australia
Published: 01:21 GMT, February 14, 2025 | Updated: 01:22 GMT, February 14, 2025
Suncorp customers will no longer be able to deposit checks in their accounts, since Australia makes the transition to online payment methods.
The bank, which has an estimate of 1.2 million members, will not accept checks at any bank branch, postcards or ATMs on Friday, February 14.
The payment method will be completely eliminated as of March 1, when checks can no longer be deposited with personal or business bank accounts.
The checks issued after March 1 will not be honored, but the writings before this date will still be processed by the bank.
Suncorp informed his clients about the changes on your website and in newspaper notices selected on Friday.
“The amendments are related to the next changes to verify the deposit services that are no longer available in Suncorp Bank and other related amendments,” said the notice.
“Suncorp Bank recommends that customers consider whether these changes will apply to their individual circumstances.”
The main bank said the decision was not taken lightly, but added that it offered customers a new opportunity to update their payment methods.
Check deposits may no longer be made to any Suncorp bank account as of February 14 and customers will no longer be able to issue checks from March 1 (shares)
Checkers will not be available after March 1 with customers to customers to crush or return any left over after this date.
The complete details of the transition far from the checks are available in a nine -page document on the Suncorp website.
It occurs after the federal government announced that check payments will be gradually eliminated by 2030.
Centerink said that I would no longer accept currency checks and money as payment methods for debt recovery on December 19, 2024.
The pensioners were informed about the transfer to the digital payment methods in the publication of Annual Pension News of Australia (APN) of the Australian services.
“If you need to pay a center debt, you must now use a different payment method, described in your debt letter,” said the update.
The checks will be gradually eliminated in a stages transition plan and will begin with government agencies and departments with ‘high control use’.
Commercial and government checks will not be issued since 2026 and the Government will stop accepting check payments in 2028.
Australia is scheduled to completely remove checks by 2030 as the country advances towards online payments (stock image)
The use of the payment method in Australia ends completely by 2030.
In the 1980s, 85 percent of all non -monetary payments were checks, but for a long time they have been surpassed by credit and debit cards, as well as direct deposits.
Australia is far behind many other countries to eliminate the use of checks, with Denmark, for example, which ends its use of checks in 2001.
Daily Mail Australia has contacted Suncorp Bank to comment.
